title: Cozy Rooftop Town Color Palette: 6 Warm Watercolor Colors with HEX Codes
desc: Six colors from my ink and watercolor painting of a busy little town: terracotta roofs, ochre walls, rust trees and rainy slate sky. Save it for your next cozy illustration. On the site you can turn any photo of your own into a palette card like this.
alt: Watercolor painting of crowded colorful houses with goats in the windows above six color swatches with names and HEX codes.
fb:
Every window in this painting has someone inside. A goat watering flowers on the roof, a goat with a fan on the balcony, a goat eating watermelon in the attic window while it snows on one side of the town and rains on the other.

When I finished it I noticed the whole thing is basically six colors: roof tile, ochre, rust, ivy green, a rainy slate blue and old brick. I pulled them out into a little palette. Which window would you live in?
grp: A trick that helped me with a very busy painting: I limited the whole piece to six colors before I started. Roofs, walls, trees and sky all come from the same six pans, mixed in different amounts. The result feels calm even with twenty windows and a crowd of characters. Next time a scene feels too chaotic, try picking your six colors first and see what happens.

title: 3-Color Christmas Palette: Tomato Red, Potion Green and Ochre (HEX Codes)
desc: A tiny Christmas palette from my watercolor of Mr. Chew the snail with a sack of presents. Three colors are enough for a whole holiday card: red, green and a warm ochre for the gold. The full palette of this painting is on my website.
alt: Watercolor snail in a Santa hat with a red sack of gifts above three color swatches: tomato red, green and ochre.
fb:
Mr. Chew does not do minimalism. Look at that sack: presents stacked higher than his shell, a candy cane, a Santa hat sliding off one eye stalk.

And still, if you squint, the whole painting is three colors. Tomato red, a slightly witchy green and ochre for everything golden. I love when a busy picture turns out to be secretly simple. Do you have a favorite Christmas color, or is it always red?
grp: If holiday cards feel like too much work, try a three-color rule: one red, one green, one warm yellow-brown. Mix the red and green together for shadows, thin the ochre for skin and gold. Everything will match automatically. It is the fastest way I know to make a small painting look finished.

ru: Палитра «Снег на старой крыше», 4 цвета (новое фото)
title: Snowy Roof Winter Color Palette: 4 Quiet Colors for Watercolor (HEX)
desc: Four quiet winter colors from a close-up of my watercolor in progress: wet bark, fresh snow, lichen grey and chimney soot. Good for snowy houses, foggy mornings and cozy winter sketches. Make your own palette from any photo on my website.
alt: Close-up of a watercolor snowy roof with glowing windows and smoking chimneys, with four winter color swatches below.
fb:
The secret of white snow in watercolor is that you do not paint it. You paint everything around it.

On this roof the snow is just bare paper. The work is in the soot on the chimneys, the grey shadows under the edges and the warm yellow in the windows that makes the cold feel colder. Four colors, a lot of leaving alone. What is harder for you: knowing what to paint or knowing what to leave white?
grp: Small watercolor tip for snowy scenes: decide where the snow is before the first wash and protect it, then paint only the shadows with a cool grey. Add one warm color, like yellow window light, and the white will suddenly look like snow instead of empty paper.

title: Cozy Winter Pixel Maze Game: Collect Ingredients, Dodge Ghosts and Brew Potions
desc: A cozy pixel game on my art website: walk your bird through a winter maze, collect snowflakes, bells and mittens, avoid the ghosts, then brew potions in the cauldron and fill your recipe book. Free with a site account, plays in the browser.
alt: Pixel art maze game on a dark blue background with a small pigeon, ghosts and winter ingredients like snowflakes and bells.
fb:
In winter Polly’s potion maze fills up with snowflakes, bells, little trees and mittens. And ghosts, who steal the last thing you picked up.

You wander through the maze, collect the ingredients, find the door and then throw everything into the cauldron to see what comes out. The recipe book slowly fills up. It is my favorite thing to play with tea when I am too tired to draw. Would you rather run from the ghosts or just collect everything slowly?
grp: Question for artists who also love games: which cozy game has the art style you would most like to learn from? I keep studying pixel games for how they show a whole world with very few details: a dark blue maze, a few glowing icons, done. Curious what inspires you.

title: 12 Cozy Things to Draw in December: Easy Winter Drawing Prompts for Your Sketchbook
desc: Twelve cozy winter drawing prompts for December: a spider knitting a scarf, cocoa, warm socks, a snow globe and more. Save the list and draw one a day. The full December list with a tip and colors for each day is on my website.
alt: Small Posca painting of a happy yellow creature in a Santa hat above a list of twelve December drawing ideas.
fb:
My favorite December prompt is “a spider is knitting a scarf”. I have no idea who suggested it, but I think about it every winter.

The little yellow fellow in the picture came out of a Posca marker session: a Santa hat, two dots for eyes and a lot of snow. That is the whole point of December prompts for me. Not perfect art, just one small cozy thing a day. Which of these twelve would you draw first?
grp: If you want a December sketch habit that actually lasts, make the prompts silly. “A spider knitting a scarf” is impossible to draw badly, so you stop worrying and just draw. Ten minutes, one object, no eraser. By the end of the month you will have a whole sketchbook of tiny winter characters.

title: 12 Slow Winter Drawing Ideas for January: Frost, Mittens, Foxes and Northern Lights
desc: A calm list of January drawing prompts: frost on the window, a red fox in the snow, patterned mittens, northern lights. Perfect for a new sketchbook in the new year. The whole January list, one theme for every day, is on my website.
alt: Watercolor sketchbook spread with blue-green poppy seed heads above a list of twelve January drawing ideas.
fb:
January is my favorite month to start a new sketchbook. Nothing is happening, the light is blue all day, and you are allowed to be slow.

This spread with dry poppy heads is exactly that mood: a few washes, some lines, no hurry. I made a list of slow January subjects to go with it, from frost on the window to a bear sleeping in its den. What is the first thing you will draw in the new year?
grp: For anyone starting a new sketchbook in January: make the first page ugly on purpose. A test swatch, a messy wash, a quick line. The fear of the white first page is real, and the fastest way out is to ruin it a little. After that, every page is just a page.

ru: Что рисовать в автобусе: 4 идеи (новые фото)
title: What to Draw on the Bus: 4 Easy Urban Sketching Ideas for Your Daily Commute
desc: Four quick urban sketching ideas from my pocket sketchbook: knitted hats, one shoe, a two-minute face, bus stop signs. Ten minutes of commute is enough. More drawing ideas for every day are on my website.
alt: Four photos of a small ink sketchbook on a bus: a woman in a knitted hat, a shoe, a quick portrait and a bus stop sign.
fb:
My sketchbook rides the bus with me every day. Most of the pages look like this: half a person, one shoe, a hat that took longer than the face.

People move, the bus shakes and the stop comes too fast. So I stopped trying to finish anything. Knitted hats are my favorite now, they hold still better than people. Do you ever draw strangers, or does it feel too awkward?
grp: Commute sketching tip: draw hats, bags and shoes first. They barely move, they have great shapes, and nobody notices you looking at their shoes. Use a pen, not a pencil, so you cannot erase. After a month of bus rides you will see your lines get faster and braver.

title: Winter Character Drawing Idea: Draw People Only by Their Hats and Coats
desc: A fun winter character drawing exercise from my sketchbook: draw a person only by their knitted hat, scarf and coat, and let the face stay simple. Great for urban sketching and cozy illustrations. More character prompts on my website.
alt: Ink sketchbook page with two figures wrapped in puffy coats and a big knitted hat, labelled winter vibes and tired alive.
fb:
In winter people turn into hats. Everything else is a coat.

On this page one person is labelled “winter vibes” and the other one “tired alive”, and honestly, that is the whole season. The hat did all the work: a huge knitted pom-pom tells you more about someone than their face. Which one are you today, winter vibes or tired alive?
grp: A character design exercise for winter: draw five people using only their hat and coat shapes. Skip the faces. You will notice how much personality fits into a pom-pom, a hood or a scarf wrapped three times. It is a great warm-up before a longer drawing session.

title: 8 Easy Holiday Doodles You Can Draw in 10 Minutes (Cozy Christmas Sketch Ideas)
desc: Eight quick holiday doodle ideas for a cozy evening: a mug with a face, a slightly burnt cookie, your pet in a paper crown. No skills needed, just a pen. More daily drawing ideas are on my website.
alt: Illustration of Pigeon Polly the bird holding brushes and a palette next to a pencil and paint tubes, above a list of eight holiday doodles.
fb:
This is Polly in full artist mode: brushes in one wing, a palette in the other, paint on her feathers and a pencil bigger than herself.

In December I am the opposite. I want tiny doodles that take ten minutes and do not need a palette at all. A mug with a face. A cookie that burnt a little. My cat in a paper crown. Which doodle would you start with tonight?
grp: When you are too tired to paint in December, doodle objects with faces. Mugs, cookies, candles. Give them two dots and a line and they become characters. It keeps the drawing habit alive on lazy evenings, and sometimes these silly doodles become the best pages of the sketchbook.

ru: Календарь декабря «Новый год в кровати» (как лучший пин)
title: New Year’s Eve in Bed with Snacks: Free Printable December Calendar Illustration
desc: The coziest way to end the year: in bed with snacks and a laptop. This illustration of Pigeon Polly is a free printable December calendar on my website, with weeks starting on Monday or Sunday.
alt: Illustration of a pigeon in a sleep mask lying in bed on New Year’s Eve with cake, a laptop and snacks.
fb:
Some people go out on New Year’s Eve. Polly gets into bed with cake, a laptop and a sleep mask pushed up on her head, just in case.

I painted her years ago and every December she comes back. This year she became a printable December calendar, so she can hang on your wall all month and remind you that staying in is a valid plan. Where will you be at midnight this year?
grp: Small composition tip from this painting: a bed seen from above is a great stage for a character. The blanket makes a big simple shape, and all the story goes around the edges: snacks, a laptop, a clock. If you want to draw a cozy scene, start with the bed and let the objects tell what kind of night it is.

title: Cozy European Christmas Eve Table Illustration: Tree, Fish, Pies and Very Odd Friends
desc: A Christmas Eve table the way it looks in many European homes: fish, little pies, a sparkling tree and everyone squeezed onto one bed. Illustration of Pigeon Polly with her friends. More of her holiday paintings are in my gallery.
alt: Illustration of a pigeon, a horse, a cat and a snail celebrating around a Christmas tree with a festive table of fish and pies.
fb:
A horse brought the champagne, the cat brought nothing and lies on the pies, the snail came in a sleep mask. Polly is the host and pretends this is all completely normal.

That is my favorite kind of holiday table: not perfect, slightly crowded, with someone you did not invite and could not imagine the evening without. Who is the “cat lying on the pies” at your holiday table?
grp: For a crowded holiday scene, give every character one small action. One holds a glass, one sleeps, one stares at the food. The viewer will read the picture like a story instead of a group photo. It also helps you decide poses quickly when there are many figures.

ru: Зимнее солнцестояние: самая длинная ночь (абстракция, новое фото)
title: Winter Solstice Watercolor Idea: Paint the Longest Night with Wet-in-Wet Blues
desc: A calm painting idea for the winter solstice, the longest night of the year: wet the paper, drop in deep blues and violets and let the blooms make the stars. My experiment is here, and more watercolor lessons are on my website.
alt: Abstract watercolor in deep blue and violet with pale round blooms that look like a night sky.
fb:
This one started as a mistake. I wet the paper too much, dropped in blue and violet and watched the water push the pigment into pale round blooms.

Normally I would panic. This time I let it dry and it looked like the night sky in December, when it gets dark before you finish lunch. On the longest night of the year I want to paint one of these again, on purpose. How do you spend the darkest evening of winter?
grp: Watercolor blooms (the round pale “cauliflowers”) happen when wetter water hits a drying wash. Usually we avoid them. Try using them: paint a dark blue wash, wait a minute, then drop clean water into it. Each drop becomes a pale circle, like a star or a snowflake. Great for night skies.

title: Send a Free Animated Pixel Art Christmas Card — Cozy Holiday E-Card, No Sign-Up
desc: A cozy pixel Christmas card with a tree, a fireplace and falling snow, animated and free to send from my art website. Pick a card, write your wish, share the link. Nice for friends far away.
alt: Pixel art Christmas card with a decorated tree, a window with snow and a fireplace in a red room.
fb:
Every December I mean to send real postcards, and every December I buy them too late.

So I made pixel ones. A tiny red room, a tree with blinking lights, snow outside the window. You write a wish, send the link, and your friend opens a little moving card. Not the same as paper, but it arrives on time. Who would you send the first one to?
grp: Pixel art tip for tiny holiday scenes: use only two or three shades for each object and one bright accent, like blinking tree lights. In a very small picture, contrast does more than detail. A dark window, a warm fireplace and one twinkle are enough to say “Christmas”.

ru: Процесс: город коз за три вечера (новые фото)
title: Ink and Watercolor Process: How I Paint a Busy Illustrated Town Step by Step
desc: My process for a detailed ink and watercolor town illustration: waterproof ink lines first, then light washes, then the darks and the details. Three stages side by side. Free watercolor lessons are on my website.
alt: Three stages of an ink and watercolor painting of a crowded town: pencil-and-ink line drawing, first color washes and the finished colorful painting.
board: How to Draw Step by Step
fb:
The first evening was only lines. Houses stacked on houses, and a goat in almost every window. At that point it looked like a coloring page and I was very tempted to stop.

The second evening was the scary one: first washes, everything pale and muddy. The third evening the darks went in and the town finally switched on. I always forget that the middle stage is supposed to look bad. Do you push through the ugly middle, or do you start something new?
grp: For detailed ink and watercolor pieces: do all the line work first with waterproof ink and let it dry overnight. Then paint from light to dark, one big area at a time. The painting will look wrong in the middle, that is normal. The last layer of darks is what makes it come together.

title: 4 Wet-in-Wet Watercolor Experiments to Try When You Don’t Know What to Paint
desc: Four abstract watercolor experiments from my studio: splatter, drips, blooms and blended stripes. No subject, no plan, just water and pigment. A great way to learn how your paints behave. Watercolor lessons on my website.
alt: Four abstract watercolor sheets: dark green splatter, turquoise drips, brown and turquoise blends and blue and brown stripes.
fb:
Some evenings I have no idea what to paint. Those evenings now produce sheets like these.

No subject at all. Just a wet sheet, too much water, a few colors that I want to understand better. One turned into drips, one into stripes, one into something that looks like a forest seen from a plane. I learn more about my paints on these nights than on “real” paintings. Would you hang one of these, or are they just practice to you?
grp: Try a “no subject” watercolor night once a week. Wet the whole sheet, choose two or three pigments and only watch what they do: which one spreads, which one sinks, which granulates. You will learn your paints faster than with any chart, and sometimes the sheet ends up being the best thing you made that week.

title: Relatable Artist Meme: Zooming In on the One Tiny Spot You Don’t Like
desc: Every artist knows this: the painting is done, everyone loves it, and you are staring at one tiny spot nobody else will notice. A watercolor close-up from my studio. More relatable art life on my website.
alt: Extreme close-up of a watercolor wall with a shiny wet spot and an ink window frame, under a meme caption.
fb:
Everyone else sees a whole town with goats in the windows. I see this. One wet spot on a wall that dried a bit too shiny.

I zoomed in on it about forty times. Then I posted the painting and nobody, not one person, mentioned it. Artists, what is the one spot in your latest piece that only you can see?
grp: Honest question for this group: how do you stop fixing a painting? I have a rule now: if I need to zoom in to see the problem, it is not a problem. Curious what your stopping rules are.

ru: Мем Полли: выпила воду для кистей
title: Watercolor Artist Meme: When You Accidentally Drink the Brush Water
desc: The most relatable watercolor accident: two glasses on the desk, one is coffee, one is paint water, and you are tired. Pigeon Polly learned the hard way. More of her life as an artist is in my gallery.
alt: Watercolor illustration of Pigeon Polly at a desk drinking from a cup of green paint water next to her coffee.
fb:
Two cups on the desk. One says “coffee”. The other one is green and has been holding brushes all evening.

Polly reached for the wrong one, and her face says everything. I painted this because it almost happened to me more than once, and I suspect I am not alone. Be honest: have you ever taken a sip of paint water?
grp: Studio safety tip that sounds silly but works: keep your paint water in a jar that looks nothing like a cup. A glass jar with a wide mouth, a different color, on the other side of the desk from your drink. Tired brains reach for the nearest mug.

title: Free Printable Year Calendar with an Illustrated Bird: Cozy Wall Planner, Week Starts Mon or Sun
desc: A free printable one-page year calendar with my illustration of Pigeon Polly’s New Year. Choose a week that starts on Monday or Sunday and print it at home. Monthly calendars and phone wallpapers are in the same Freebies section.
alt: Illustrated one-page year calendar with a pigeon celebrating New Year on top and twelve small months below.
fb:
I like to see the whole year at once. Twelve tiny months on one page, stuck on the fridge, slowly getting crossed out.

So the New Year painting of Polly became a one-page calendar. It is free to download, and you can choose if your week starts on Monday or Sunday, because apparently that is a big debate. Which camp are you in?
grp: A small planning habit that helps me with art goals: one printed year calendar, and a dot on every day I drew at least ten minutes. No apps, no streaks to break, just dots. By March you can see your rhythm, and the empty weeks are surprisingly motivating.

title: Free Cozy Winter Printables: Illustrated Monthly Calendars and Phone Wallpapers
desc: Free cozy winter downloads from my art website: illustrated monthly calendars for December and January and phone wallpapers with my paintings. Print at home or set as your lock screen.
alt: Four free downloads: a January calendar with a bird, a December calendar with a snail, a cat with fairy lights and a mushroom house wallpaper.
fb:
January calendar: Polly stays in, wrapped up, with no plans at all. December calendar: Mr. Chew drags a sack of presents bigger than his shell.

I put them both on the site for free, together with phone wallpapers made from my paintings. I like the idea that someone checks the date and sees a snail working harder than them. Which one would you put on your wall?
grp: If you paint, turn your favorite piece into a calendar page for yourself. Seeing your own art every day for a month is a quiet confidence boost, and you will notice what you would change next time. It works even with a home printer.

title: Advent Calendar with Limited Items: 62 Cozy Things Hidden Behind the Doors
desc: My website has an advent calendar with a twist: every window hides two limited items for your room that cannot be bought, gifted or sold, only found. Read how it works in the site news.
alt: Preview image of an advent calendar on a website with winter windows and small hidden items.
fb:
There are 62 things on my website that you cannot buy. Not with buttons, not as a gift, not from other players.

They are hidden in the advent calendar, two in every window, and the only way to get them is to open the door on the right day. I liked the idea of something small that you simply had to be there for. Do you open advent windows every morning, or all at once at the end?
grp: For anyone who makes advent calendars or daily art challenges: the magic is in scarcity, not size. One small thing a day that disappears if you miss it feels more special than a big reward at the end. Worth trying for your own audience or even just your sketchbook.

ru: Новости сайта: зимний пир и гости
title: Cozy Winter Feast in a Pixel Bird Market: Visit Other Players’ Rooms and Play Together
desc: New on my website: a long winter table at the Bird Market with dumplings, punch, snowdrifts and ice sculptures. And now your bird can appear in someone else’s room and play there. Read the site news.
alt: Pixel art winter market with a long festive table, snowdrifts and ice sculptures.
fb:
The Bird Market got a winter table this month. A long one, with dumplings, punch and ice sculptures between the snowdrifts.

And something I wanted for a long time: your bird can now show up in someone else’s room and play there. Like knocking on a neighbor’s window. It is a small thing, but it makes the site feel less like a website and more like a little town. Would you rather host or visit?
grp: Pixel art question for the group: when you draw food in very low resolution, what helps you most? For the dumplings on this table I used one highlight pixel and a darker outline only on the bottom. Curious how others make tiny food look tasty.

title: How to Choose a Sketchbook: Paper, Size and Binding Explained Simply
desc: Hundreds of sketchbooks on the shelf and no idea where to start? My blog article walks through paper weight, size and binding so you can pick one you will actually use. Photo of my watercolor sketchbook with rosehips.
alt: Small watercolor sketchbook open on a page with rosehip branches, next to paints and markers, with a ginger cat behind it.
fb:
This sketchbook has survived coffee, a bus, a cat sitting on it and a whole autumn of rosehips.

People often ask me which sketchbook to buy, and the honest answer is: the one you are not afraid to ruin. I wrote down everything I look for, from paper weight to binding, in a blog post. What is the one thing a sketchbook must have for you?
grp: Sketchbook tip: if you paint with watercolor even sometimes, look for paper that is at least 200 gsm, and a binding that opens flat. Size matters less than you think. Pick the size that fits your bag, because the best sketchbook is the one you carry.

title: Wobbleland: Explore a Cozy Pixel Fantasy Map with 11 Towns, Holidays and Recipes
desc: Wobbleland is the little fantasy country on my website: a pixel map with eleven towns, each with its own coat of arms, holidays and recipes. A cozy place to wander and get ideas for drawing.
alt: Pixel art fantasy map of Wobbleland with small towns, rivers and forests.
fb:
Somewhere between my sketchbook and my website there is a small country called Wobbleland.

It has eleven towns, and each one got its own coat of arms, its own holidays and its own recipes. I keep adding things whenever a town tells me something new about itself. If you could add one holiday to an invented country, what would people celebrate?
grp: Worldbuilding tip for illustrators: give every place one holiday and one recipe. Suddenly you know what people wear, eat and decorate, and you have twenty drawing prompts for free. It works for comics, games or just a sketchbook series.

ru: Норвежский: слова в скетчбуке в автобусе (новое фото)
title: Learning a Language Through Sketching: Norwegian Words in My Bus Sketchbook
desc: I am learning Norwegian and my sketchbook comes along: a few lines in Norwegian next to quick ink sketches of the bus stop and a shoe. Drawing helps the words stick. More sketchbook pages are in my gallery.
alt: Small ink sketchbook on a bus with handwritten Norwegian sentences, a sketch of a shoe and a bus stop sign.
fb:
I am learning Norwegian, slowly, mostly on the bus.

On this page a few Norwegian lines sit right next to a shoe and a bus stop sign. I remember words better when they share a page with a drawing, because later I remember the drawing first and the word follows. Have you ever learned a language in a strange way that actually worked?
grp: Language learning tip for people who draw: write new words on the same page as a quick sketch of where you are. The memory of the place helps you recall the word. It turns any sketchbook into a vocabulary notebook without extra effort.

title: 6 Cozy Norwegian Winter Words to Learn and Draw: Koselig, Lue, Votter and More
desc: Six cozy Norwegian winter words with meanings, perfect for a sketchbook page: koselig, lue, votter, snø, kakao, pepperkake. Draw each one and the words stick. Illustration of Pigeon Polly’s cozy night in.
alt: Illustration of a pigeon resting at home on a winter night above a list of six Norwegian winter words with English meanings.
fb:
My favorite Norwegian word so far is “koselig”. It means cozy, but bigger: candles, wool socks, someone making kakao in the kitchen.

I collect winter words like this and draw them, because a drawn word stays with me longer. Lue is a knitted hat, votter are mittens, pepperkake is gingerbread. Polly’s January night in feels very koselig to me. Do you have a word in your language for this feeling?
grp: Drawing prompt with a twist: pick six winter words in a language you are learning and draw one per day. Lue, votter, snø — a hat, mittens, snow. It is a gentle prompt list and a vocabulary lesson at the same time.

title: Watercolor Sketches: Creative Guide — an E-Book for Loose, Cozy Watercolor Sketching
desc: My e-book Watercolor Sketches: Creative Guide, for anyone who wants to sketch with watercolor in a loose, relaxed way. All my art e-books, including a free coloring book, are listed on my website.
alt: Cover of the e-book Watercolor Sketches: Creative Guide with watercolor illustrations.
fb:
Winter is when I finally read the art books I bought in summer.

If you are like me, maybe this one fits your stack: my guide to watercolor sketching, made for people who want loose, quick pages instead of perfect paintings. There is also a free coloring book on the same page if you just want to relax. What is on your winter reading pile?
grp: Question for the group: what was the one book or tutorial that changed how you sketch? For me it was the idea that a sketch does not need to be finished, only true. Would love a list of favorites for winter reading.

ru: Мой набор: акварель в коробочке от мятных конфет (как лучший пост FB)
title: DIY Pocket Watercolor Kit in a Mint Tin: Tiny Travel Art Setup for Urban Sketching
desc: My tiniest travel art kit: a mint tin with a few watercolor half pans, a water brush pen and a pocket sketchbook with stickers. Fits in any coat pocket for winter sketching. More sketching tips on my website.
alt: An open mint tin with watercolor pans, a water brush pen and a small black sketchbook with stickers on a wooden table.
fb:
This is everything I need to paint outside the house. A mint tin with a few pans of watercolor, a brush pen with water inside and a tiny sketchbook covered in stickers.

It fits in a coat pocket, which in winter matters more than anything. I like that it forces me to choose: only these colors today, only this page. What is the one art tool you never leave home without?
grp: How to make a pocket watercolor kit: take an empty mint tin, glue in a few empty half pans with a drop of glue or magnets, fill them with tube paint and let it dry overnight. Add a water brush pen and the smallest sketchbook you have. Choose a limited palette, it will make your sketches more harmonious.

ru: Мой набор: выкраски, кисти, тесты (новые фото)
title: Watercolor Artist Studio Essentials: Swatched Palette, Brushes and Test Pages
desc: A honest look at my watercolor studio: a palette with every color swatched and labelled on the lid, brushes in a pumpkin mug, test strokes before each painting and several palettes open at once. Watercolor lessons on my website.
alt: Four studio photos: a watercolor palette with labelled swatches, brushes in an orange pumpkin mug, a sketchbook with test strokes and a desk full of palettes.
fb:
Behind every finished painting there is a desk that looks like this.

A palette with every color swatched and labelled on the lid, because I never remember which green is which. Brushes living in a pumpkin mug since October. A page of test strokes before I touch the real paper. And at least three palettes open at once, for no good reason. What does your desk look like right now?
grp: Most useful 15 minutes in watercolor: swatch every color in your palette on a strip of the same paper you paint on, and write the pigment code under it. Stick it inside the lid. You will stop guessing, mix cleaner and finally understand why two “blues” behave so differently.

ru: Северная зима: 8 вещей при свечах (новое фото)
title: Cozy Nordic Winter Painting Ideas: 8 Slow Hygge Things to Paint by Candlelight
desc: Eight slow, cozy Nordic winter painting ideas: one lit window in a dark house, chimney smoke, clementines, a sleeping cat on a blanket. Perfect for quiet evenings with watercolor. More winter prompts on my website.
alt: Watercolor in progress of snowy rooftops and chimneys with warm windows above a list of eight cozy winter painting ideas.
fb:
In the north the winter evenings start at four. I used to hate it, now I paint through it.

The best subjects are the slow ones: one lit window in a dark house, smoke from a chimney, a sock drying on the radiator. In this painting the snowy roofs came first and the warm windows last, and the whole town switched on like a real evening. What is the coziest thing you can see from your window right now?
grp: Painting tip for winter evenings: paint one warm light source in an otherwise cool scene. A yellow window, a candle, a lamp. Keep everything else blue and grey. The contrast makes the picture feel cozy instantly, even with very simple drawing.

title: Cozy New Year’s Eve Mood: Cooking Dinner in Bed Because the Kitchen Is Too Far
desc: The most relatable New Year’s Eve: chopping salad in bed, a laptop with a movie, a sleep mask ready for midnight. Illustration of Pigeon Polly’s pyjama party. More of her cozy life in my gallery.
alt: Illustration of a pigeon in bed on December 31 cutting vegetables on a board, with a laptop, a clock and a calendar page.
fb:
The calendar on the wall says 31. Polly is in bed, chopping salad on a board on her knees, a movie on the laptop and a sleep mask on standby.

She calls it a pyjama party. I call it the most honest New Year’s Eve I have ever painted. Some years you go out, some years you make the bed your whole kitchen. What does your perfect December 31 look like?
grp: Composition idea for cozy illustrations: put a calendar page or a clock somewhere in the background. One small number, like 31, tells the whole story of the scene without any words. It is a simple trick to turn an everyday room into a specific moment.
